title: Normalized derived adjunction from a resolving class
statement: Let A and B be abelian categories with independently chosen unbounded derived localizations [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let E:A to B and R:B to A be additive, E left adjoint to R, and R exact. Let P be a predicate on cochain complexes of A such that every complex admits a quasi-isomorphism Y to X from P, and E applied termwise preserves quasi-isomorphisms between P-complexes. Then E on complexes followed by localization has a pointwise left derived functor L with universal counit epsilon, invertible on P-complexes. Moreover L is left adjoint to the exact termwise derived R. For every chain map f:E X to K, the derived adjunct of epsilon_X followed by Q(f) is Q of the ordinary complex adjunct, followed by the inverse of the fixed derived-restriction factorization. The transpose formula holds for all complexes X, not just resolving objects.

proof.text: Pass to the homotopy quotient. Represent the resolving class there by complexes satisfying P; fullness of the quotient lifts its morphisms. The given preservation hypothesis makes their images invertible after localization. Apply the resolving-class left-derived existence theorem.

Quasi-isomorphisms form a saturated system with calculi of fractions. Resolving-class essential constancy gives the left derived pro-diagrams. Exactness makes the restriction ind-diagrams essentially constant. Apply the normalized derived-adjunction compatibility theorem.

Precompose the pointwise Kan extension with the full essentially surjective homotopy quotient, which is initial on the relevant comma categories. Transport along the quotient/localization factorization isomorphisms. Their components are identities; the homotopy adjunction descends the cochain transpose, giving the displayed formula.

theorem exists_leftDerived_adjunction
    (E : A ⥤ B) (R : B ⥤ A) [E.Additive] [R.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits R] [PreservesFiniteColimits R] (a : E ⊣ R)
    (P : CochainComplex A ℤ → Prop)
    (hres : ∀ X : CochainComplex A ℤ, ∃ (Y : CochainComplex A ℤ) (s : Y ⟶ X),
      P Y ∧ QuasiIso s)
    (hpres : ∀ {X Y : CochainComplex A ℤ} (f : X ⟶ Y), P X → P Y → QuasiIso f →
      QuasiIso ((E.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map f)) :
    (E.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q).HasPointwiseLeftDerivedFunctor
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso A (.up ℤ)) ∧
    ∃ (L : DerivedCategory A ⥤ DerivedCategory B)
      (ε : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ L ⟶ E.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q),
      L.IsLeftDerivedFunctor ε (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso A (.up ℤ)) ∧
      (∀ X, P X → IsIso (ε.app X)) ∧
      ∃ d : L ⊣ R.mapDerivedCategory, ∀ X K
        (f : (E.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj X ⟶ K),
        d.homEquiv (DerivedCategory.Q.obj X) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)
          (ε.app X ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map f) =
        DerivedCategory.Q.map ((a.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).homEquiv X K f) ≫
          R.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app K
